core_obligations: Choose a representative (proof lines 4336-4337): let I^bullet be a K-injective complex of O-modules representing K.

Identify the section complexes (proof lines 4338-4341): by construction of cohomology, H^q(U, K) = H^q(Gamma(U, I^bullet)), and this equals H^q(Gamma(C/U, I^bullet|_{C/U})) because sections of the restriction over the localized site are sections over U.
Conclude (proof lines 4342-4345): by the same-chapter result, I^bullet|_{C/U} is a K-injective complex representing K|_{C/U}, so the displayed cohomology is exactly H^q(C/U, K|_{C/U}).
proof_roadmap: Represent K by a K-injective complex.
Cohomology at U is the cohomology of the section complex over U, which is the section complex over the localized site C/U.
The restriction of a K-injective complex to C/U stays K-injective and represents the restriction of K.
Hence the two cohomology groups agree.
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the cohomology of an object of D(O) at an object U of a ringed site with the cohomology of its restriction on the localized site C/U (statement lines 4328-4333). The proof is a two-line unfolding of the definition of cohomology after choosing a K-injective representative I^bullet, so that both sides become the cohomology of the same section complex, together with the same-chapter observation that restriction to C/U preserves K-injectivity and represents the restricted object (proof lines 4336-4345). The claim is H2: one representative choice and one identification of section complexes.
